opening.headline: I pasted the entire manual, and it explains why the assistant behaves erratically in a structure of instructions, knowledge, and tools, and covers how to fix it.
body: I pasted the entire 40-page in-house response manual into the assistant’s instructions section. However, when I inquired about a refund, they recited the personnel regulations at the front of the manual, and their tone fluctuated, sometimes giving long and sometimes short answers. The problem is often not the model, but the way the instructions are structured.

In this lesson, we'll first see that custom assistants like GPTs and Gems are made up of three parts: instructions, knowledge, and tools. We then look at how to turn manuals into structured instructions, the criteria for dividing instructions and knowledge files, and the path to moving GPT into a plugin. At the end, we explain cases where two lines of conflicting instructions cause malfunctions and cases where the boundary between instructions and knowledge is blurred.

As of 2026-10: Custom GPT is a feature moving to a plugin. The GPT builder example below is an explanation for understanding and migrating existing workflows. Please check the workspace notice for new creation possibilities and termination schedules. After transferring instructions and knowledge files, custom actions and results must be verified separately.

As of 2026-10: Gems are transitioning to skills. Personal accounts will be converted after November 2026, and Workspace business accounts will be converted after March 2027. The Gems screen below is based on the pre-migration environment. After moving the instructions and files, please check again for sharing and tool operation.

visual.alt: A screen with a long manual attached entirely to the instructions section and a response card that answers refund questions with personnel regulations.
labels: How do I get a refund?
Hello, customer. Every reception begins with a greeting.

paragraphs: The customer center team leader pasted the entire in-house response manual into the assistant’s instructions section. The manual includes personnel policy, refund policy, tone of voice policy, refundable items, and answer length policy. I expected that the assistant would now take care of it.

However, in response to the question, ‘How do I get a refund?’, the assistant recited the personnel regulations at the front of the manual. The tone fluctuated, sometimes as short as a single sentence, and sometimes as long explanations of the procedure. This is because the manual contained conflicting sentences such as ‘always brief’ and ‘detailed guidance’.

A manual is written for people to read and judge according to the situation. The assistant's guidelines are rules of conduct that the model must follow in all conversations. The question for this class is this. How can I change the manual so that the assistant works as intended?

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: People notice the contradiction between ‘always keep it short’ and ‘give detailed information’ and judge it based on the situation. How would the model behave without that criterion?

screens.outro: Now that we have established that the crux of the problem lies in the structure of the guidelines, let us recall your experience.

screens.title: Recall the guidelines I made
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think for yourself first and then click.

items.prompt: Have you ever written a lengthy explanation of your role to AI and wanted to rewrite it?
items.answer: That's why the custom assistant was created. You can write down roles and rules once in GPT or Gem, and then load those settings for each new conversation. In this lesson, you'll learn how to configure that setting to ensure it works as intended.

items.prompt: Have you ever felt that the more instructions you give, the less you listen to them?
items.answer: As the number of instructions increases, it is easy for sentences to conflict with each other. When there are conflicting sentences, the model sways its response to follow the other in each situation. This is why structure and priorities are important, not the amount of guidance.

items.prompt: If you were to create a helper for the same team to use, what would you like to tell them?
items.answer: Usually, a mixture of two types of content comes to mind. One is the rule, ‘Act like this,’ and the other is the fact, ‘Refer to this material.’ Dividing these two is the central theme of this class.

screens.outro: First, let's look at the components of a custom assistant.

screens.title: GPTs and Gems: Three Parts: Instructions, Knowledge, and Tools
screens.lead: Select the number marker above the picture to see a detailed description of the parts that make up your custom assistant.

visual.alt: A schematic with instructions, knowledge, tools, and conversation starters linked to the central assistant icon.

markers.label: instructions
markers.title: Rules of conduct that apply to all conversations
markers.body: OpenAI's GPT components consist of a name, description, conversation starter, instructions, knowledge, features and connected apps. Guidelines are rules that determine how GPT behaves and responds, and apply to all conversations. You must also create a gem with a name and instructions, check its operation in the preview on the right, and then save it for it to be reflected. Just previewing doesn't save it.

markers.label: knowledge
markers.title: Reference materials to use when answering
markers.body: Knowledge is the reference material that the assistant uses when answering. In GPT, you upload knowledge files, and in Gem, you add files from Knowledge. The difference is that while instructions are rules that must always be followed, knowledge is facts that can be retrieved when needed.

markers.label: tools
markers.title: Features and Connected Apps
markers.body: Tools are features and connected apps that allow your assistant to do things outside of your guidance and knowledge. Turn on the required features in GPT settings and connect the app. The more tools you can turn on, the more convenient it is, but it's important to write down which tool to use and when in your instructions so your assistant doesn't get confused.

markers.label: Conversation Starter Phrases
markers.title: Example questions the user first sees
markers.body:
The conversation starter text is an example prompt you see when you open GPT. Let users know what they can ask and make it easy to start a conversation. If the name and description are your clues to finding and understanding GPT, conversation starters are your clues to how to use it.

Also know how to make it. GPT creation is done on the web and can only be used on mobile devices. Personal ChatGPT accounts cannot create or publish new GPTs, and can only be created with permission in Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspaces. When creating, choose between an interactive builder that creates a draft with verbal instructions, or a settings screen that allows you to modify items directly.

screens.outro: Now that you've seen the components, let's see what good guidelines look like with a before and after comparison.

screens.title: How instructions and knowledge are delivered to the model, and why responses vary
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about the differences in how instructions and knowledge enter the model, why responses to the same question vary, and the priorities between instructions.

visual.alt: A schematic where a request made to a model is assembled from instructions, retrieved knowledge fragments, conversation history, and a new question, resulting in two different responses from the same request.
labels: Knowledge fragments retrieved (varies for each question)
Model (selects the next horse with probability)

tabs.label: Instructions: Instructions delivered together every time.
tabs.body:
Instructions are instructions that are given to the model in every conversation with the assistant. The understanding is that no matter what the user asks, the same instructions are anchored and followed at the beginning of the request. That's why I say, 'It applies to all conversations.'

Since the scope of how instructions are laid out internally varies from product to product, the detailed method cannot be determined. However, the role of ‘instructions delivered together every time’ is the same.

Instructions also take up the amount the model reads at a time, or context window. The longer and more verbose the instructions, the less space there is for data and conversation, and the more room for conflict between sentences.

tabs.label: Knowledge: Materials selected for each question
tabs.body:
A knowledge file is material that is added to the request by searching for parts that seem necessary when a question comes in. If you have a lot of data, only pieces will come in, not the whole thing. So, depending on the wording of the question or search results, the same content may come in at times and be left out at other times.

This is the principle behind the saying, 'If you put it in a knowledge file, there is no guarantee that it will always be applied.' Things that must be followed every time, such as rules about using polite language, are placed in guidelines, and facts that can be brought up only when necessary are placed in knowledge.

tabs.label: Why responses vary
tabs.body:
The language model continues the sentence by selecting the next word from a probability distribution. There is a stochastic element in the selection process, so the expression and composition may vary for the same input. It is not a whim, but a nature of how it is created.

Clearer instructions narrow the range of possible responses, resulting in smaller differences. Conversely, if there are conflicting statements in the instructions, which one to follow may vary from run to run. You can write down the selection criteria by adding conditions such as 'general inquiries are short, procedural inquiries are numbered steps', and by asking the same question several times in the preview, you can find the point where you are shaky.

tabs.label: Priority between instructions
tabs.body:
The instructions given to the model can come from several sources. System instructions established by the service provider, instructions written by the assistant creator, requests entered by the user in conversations, and text taken from tools or documents are all mixed in.

Model developers train their models to prioritize instructions from higher authorities. Wallace et al.'s research called this an instruction hierarchy and proposed a method of teaching children to follow higher-level instructions when they conflict with lower-level instructions.

However, this priority addresses issues between instructions from different sources. Problems where two sentences in the same guideline conflict must be resolved by the writer themselves. The specific implementation of product-specific priorities is beyond the scope of disclosure and cannot be determined.

screens.outro: Now that you know the delivery method, let's compare how to turn a manual into instructions.

ext.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions (Wallace et al.)

screens.title: Instruction Writing: Turning Manuals into Guidelines
screens.lead: Switch between the two states and compare how the original text of the manual changes into structured instructions.

visual.alt: An illustration in which the original text of the manual on the left is rearranged into instructions in four areas: roles, tasks, background, and format on the right.

states.label: Original text of manual
states.body:
The instructions, copied directly from the manual, look like this.

```
Refund Inquiry Response Manual (excerpt)

1. Greeting policy: All responses begin with “Hello, customer.”
2. Refund Policy: Refunds can be requested within 14 days of purchase.
3. Tone rule: Always use polite language.
4. List of refundable items: clothing, general merchandise, small home appliances.
5. Answer length: Always answer briefly, one sentence.
6. Procedure guidance: Provide detailed step-by-step guidance to customers through the procedure.
```

There are three problems here: First, there is a conflict between No. 5 ‘Always one sentence’ and No. 6 ‘Detailed instructions’. Second, rules (1, 3, 5, 6) and facts (2, 4) are mixed in the same list. Third, there is no order or condition as to which rule should be applied first to which question. People make judgments based on the situation, but models obtain the basis for this judgment only from guidelines.

states.label: changed to guidelines
states.body:
OpenAI's instructions tell you to write multi-step flows with explicit steps, such as 'If Prioritize positive, specific 'do this' instructions rather than a list of prohibitions, and if definitions or classifications are needed, briefly include examples of acceptable and unacceptable output. It is also recommended to make priorities and steps visible through titles and lists.

The gem creation guide presents four areas: Persona, Task, Context, and Format, and tells you that you only need to use a few of them.

```
## Role
You are a customer service representative responding to refund inquiries.

## to do
- Answer general inquiries briefly in one or two sentences.
- Inquiries regarding refund procedures will be guided to numbered steps.

## background
You can apply for a refund within 14 days of purchase.

## Format
Always use polite language and answer the question directly in the first sentence.
```

The two conflicting sentences were changed to the following conditions: ‘General inquiries should be brief, and procedural inquiries should be numbered.’ Now the type of question determines which rules to follow.

screens.outro: Now that we have compared before and after, let's look at the criteria for dividing knowledge files and instructions.

screens.title: Knowledge files vs. instructions, tool connections
screens.lead: If you select an underlined sentence in the manual below, you can check whether that sentence should be used as guidance or knowledge and why.

visual.alt: An illustration showing the instruction and knowledge sections side by side and the manual sentences moving from one to the other.

data.text: Refund inquiry response manual. All responses begin with “Hello, customer.”. Refunds can be requested within 14 days of purchase.. Always use polite language. Refundable items include clothing, miscellaneous goods, and small home appliances.. General inquiries are answered briefly in one or two sentences. Please refer to the separate file for the price list..

marks.note: Go to instructions. These are rules that determine how to behave. These rules should apply to all conversations, so we leave them as guidelines.

marks.span: Refunds can be requested within 14 days of purchase.
marks.note: Go to knowledge. This is a fact I bring up when answering. When periods change, it is easier to manage by changing the contents of the knowledge file rather than revising the instructions.
Go to instructions. Rules about tone should apply to all responses. Because knowledge files are retrieved for each question, there is no guarantee that they will always be applied to all responses.

marks.span: Refundable items include clothing, miscellaneous goods, and small home appliances.
marks.note: Go to knowledge. Item list is indicative and subject to change. Keeping the list as a knowledge file makes it easy to update.

marks.span: Please refer to the separate file for the price list.
marks.note: This is a sentence that points to a file. The price list itself is uploaded as a knowledge file, and the instructions include only what questions to refer to the file for.

screens.outro: Now that we've separated the parts, let's look at practical tips and transition paths when dealing with knowledge files.

screens.title: Knowledge file tips and GPT conversion/migration
screens.lead: Select the arrows to move through each step to check tips for uploading knowledge files and the inspection sequence when moving GPT to a plugin.

steps.title: File limits and formats
steps.body: You can attach up to 20 knowledge files to GPT, up to 512MB per file. Some file types require Code Interpreter & Data Analysis to be enabled. Simple, text-centric files are easier to read than files with complex layouts.

steps.title: Quotes and Previews
steps.body: If you want to cite a source in your answer, write the citation format in the instructions. After uploading a file, ask questions in the preview to see if the Assistant is writing the file as intended. When you add a Drive file to your Gem, it uses the latest version and therefore reflects your original modifications.

steps.title: Flow of moving to plug-in
steps.body: OpenAI guides you through a migration flow to move your custom GPT into a plugin. Plugins bundle together reusable instructions, reference files, and connected apps. Gems also provide guidance on the conversion path to skills. Both involve putting the same parts—instructions, knowledge, and tools—in a new form.

steps.title: Check before moving
steps.body: The creator of GPT first checks three things: instructions, reference files, and connecting apps. Migration is based on the latest published version of GPT, so drafts and unpublished edits are not moved. Integrations you create yourself, such as custom actions, are not automatically moved and require more time to prepare.

steps.title: Test after moving
steps.body: After completing the migration, review the transferred instructions and reference files and test the replacement using your usual tasks. It's a good idea to save a few familiar prompts in advance for comparison. After migration, the original GPT becomes read-only, so make any necessary modifications before moving it.

steps.title: Cases of using someone else’s GPT and function blocks
steps.body: Anyone using a GPT created by someone else will see alternative methods guided by the creator. Meanwhile, ChatGPT's writing block and code block are features that allow you to edit and preview drafts and code directly within the response. Separate from the custom assistant, this is a tool that continues operations within the response.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen how to switch, we'll explain examples of conflicting guidelines.

screens.title: Case Description 1: Malfunction caused by two lines of conflicting instructions
screens.lead: An instructor breaks down how two conflicting lines of instructions cause misbehavior. Select the arrows to follow step by step.

steps.title: two lines colliding
steps.body: Inside the long instructions are two lines spaced far apart from each other. Line 12 is ‘Always give a short answer in one sentence’, and line 47 is ‘Guide the customer through the process in detail step by step.’ The author was not conscious of the contradictions between each line as he wrote them.

steps.title: change in response
steps.body: If you send the question ‘How do I get a refund?’ several times, sometimes they will reply in one sentence and sometimes they will give you a long explanation of the steps. The different responses to the same question are not because the model is capricious, but because the instructions ask for both.

steps.title: cause
steps.body: There is no precedence in the instructions, so the model follows one in each situation. Generative models can respond differently to the same input, so which of the two rules is reflected more strongly varies each time. The longer the instructions, the more difficult it is to detect these conflicts.

steps.title: amendment
steps.body: Append a condition to two conflicting lines. 'Respond briefly to general inquiries in one or two sentences. Inquiries regarding procedures are guided through numbered steps.' Now the two rules apply to different question types so they don't conflict.

steps.title: Confirm after editing
steps.body: After fixing it, check the behavior for each question type in Preview. Ask ‘How long does delivery take?’ and ‘How do I get a refund?’ and see if you answer the first question briefly and the second question in numerical steps. Having the before and after instructions side by side makes it easy to record what's changed.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the structure of conflict, let's look at an example of when the line between guidance and knowledge is blurred.

screens.title: Case Commentary 2: When the boundary between guidance and knowledge is blurred
screens.lead: When you select an inspection item, the cause of the problem and the direction to take will be revealed. First, decide for yourself where to move it and then click it.

items.prompt: Situation 1: You attach a price list to the guidelines, but you have to update the guidelines every time the price changes.
items.answer: Move frequently changing reference materials to a knowledge file. Modifying the guidelines is a burden because it affects the assistant's entire behavior. Knowledge files can be replaced with new versions, and if it is a Drive file added to the Gem, the latest version can be used simply by modifying the original.

items.prompt: Situation 2: Rules such as ‘Be sure to use polite language’ are mixed in the knowledge file.
items.answer: Move rules into guidelines and leave only facts as knowledge. The sentences in the knowledge file are a reference to look for and read when answering, and are not guaranteed to be rules of conduct that apply to all conversations at all times. If there is a rule that must be followed, it should be in the instructions.

items.prompt: Situation 3: The same sentence is duplicated in instructions and knowledge.
items.answer: Duplication can cause conflicting statements when only one side is modified. Keep one sentence in only one place. If it is a behavioral rule, it is placed in a guideline; if it is a fact, it is placed in knowledge; and in the guideline, only the location is indicated, such as 'refer to the price list file for prices.'

items.prompt: How do I do the final inspection?
items.answer: Check the action with three questions in the preview. One question asks whether the rules are applied, one question asks about the contents of the knowledge file, and one question overlaps the two. If it is different from the intention, we first question whether the sentence is a guideline or knowledge. Also remember that gems will not be reflected until you preview and save them.

screens.outro: Now that we've finished the case, let's summarize the main points of this lesson.

screens.title: Rules are guidelines, facts are knowledge
screens.lead: Let's summarize the content covered in this class by connecting it to the first question.

paragraphs: The first question was how to change the manual so that the assistant would work as intended. The answer lies in breaking down the manual. How to act is included in the instructions, what to refer to is included in the knowledge file, and necessary functions are linked to tools. These three parts are the structure of a custom assistant.

Instructions write steps and conditions in detail, such as 'If Positive instructions are given priority over prohibition lists, and conflicting statements are resolved by adding conditions. Only facts are kept in knowledge files, and the more frequently changing data is placed in knowledge rather than guidelines.

The form of a custom assistant may change. OpenAI provides guidance on moving GPT to plugins, and Google provides guidance on moving Gems to skills. Even if the format changes, the structure of instructions, knowledge, and tools remains the same, so checking these three things before moving makes the transition easier.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: Every time you write a sentence, ask first, ‘Is this a rule of conduct or a fact to refer to?’

checks.q: When I added the sentence 'Always use polite language' only in the knowledge file, some of the answers ended up using informal language. What is the most appropriate cause and response?
options: Since knowledge is data retrieved for each question, there may have been requests missing that sentence, so the rules are translated into guidelines.
The model cannot read the knowledge file, so reupload the file
Instructions are always weaker than knowledge, so greater emphasis is placed on statements of knowledge.
Because the response is probabilistic, no response is effective.
checks.explain: Instructions are delivered with each request, and knowledge is retrieved only for the pieces you need. Rules that must be followed should be included in the guidelines.

glossary.def: This is a customized assistant created by ChatGPT that bundles instructions, knowledge, and functions.
A custom assistant created by Gemini with instructions and files. You must save it after previewing for it to be reflected.
These are the rules that determine how your assistant will behave and respond. Applies to all conversations.
This is information that the assistant can refer to when answering questions.
This is a conversion procedure to move GPT to a plug-in, etc. After moving, the original becomes read-only.

The concept is to ensure that when instructions from different sources conflict, such as system instructions, producer instructions, or user requests, instructions from a higher authority take precedence.

misconceptions.myth: It is most accurate to attach the entire manual.
misconceptions.fact: The Assistant falters when rules and references get mixed up and you end up with conflicting sentences. Rules must be divided into guidelines and data must be divided into knowledge for things to move as intended.

misconceptions.myth: The longer the prohibited list, the safer it is.
misconceptions.fact: Positive, specific ‘do this’ instructions are better followed than a list of don’ts. You can also add short examples of acceptable and unacceptable output.

misconceptions.myth: Even if you put a rule in a knowledge file, it is applied the same way as a guideline.
misconceptions.fact: Knowledge files are reference materials to look for and read when answering questions. Rules that must always be followed must be placed in guidelines, and facts must be placed in knowledge to ensure clear boundaries.

misconceptions.myth: If the answers to the same question are different, the assistant is broken.
misconceptions.fact: Because the model selects words probabilistically to create sentences, the expression may vary even with the same input. Clear instructions and eliminating conflicting statements reduce wobble.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: A custom assistant consists of instructions, knowledge, and tools.
Guidelines contain rules of conduct, knowledge files contain reference material, and do not mix the two.
Resolve conflicting instructions with conditions and check each question type in the preview.
Before moving a GPT to a plugin, check the instructions, files, and associated apps.
